subject: Segregated-processing and derivative controls for LLM outputs
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@medisys.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Segregated-processing and derivative controls for LLM outputs

Hi Alex / Laura,

Thanks for taking this. Our legal and security teams reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and flagged two high-level concerns for Medisys:

1) We need a firm commitment that customer prompts and model responses for Medisys accounts will not be used to improve Redwood-hosted models (including internal research models) without explicit opt-in.
2) We need operational proof points for how Redwood segments customer data at rest and in-flight, and which subprocessors may touch unredacted prompt/response pairs.

I've attached a short list of questions (Medisys_DPA_Questions.pdf) and we also have an initial redline from legal coming in this afternoon. Key ask: can you provide a short operational playbook (controls, retention, KMS options, subprocessor list + residency) and confirm whether derivatives (e.g., aggregated fine-tuning data) are expressly prohibited?

We'd like to avoid a long procurement loop if possible — a pragmatic plan + evidence pack should let our InfoSec sign off. Would you be available for a 30-min sync today?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Platform Security, Medisys

Attachments: Medisys_DPA_Questions.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@medisys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Segregated-processing and derivative controls for LLM outputs

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Rishi from Product Compliance so we can give concrete operational answers. Quick answers up front:

- No implicit model improvement: for "hosted API" customers we offer a documented opt-in flow for model tuning. By default, account-specific prompts/responses are not fed back into our public models. We can commit to a contractual "no-use-for-improvement" clause subject to technical evidence and the DPA wording.

- Segregation & subprocessors: we maintain per-tenant isolation at the serving layer (ephemeral KV caches scoped per customer), and we can provide a list of subprocessors that have potential access to raw request logs. We also support Dedicated/Private deployment where data never leaves customer-networked deployment.

Next steps I propose:
- We'll share an "operational playbook" (controls, retention, KV behavior, KMS options, subprocessor list) by EOD — that will include sample logs/fields we retain and retention windows.
- We can review Medisys' redline when it arrives and propose trackable language that maps to the playbook.
- If helpful, we can run a 30-min session with your InfoSec and ours this afternoon — Rishi / Laura, are you available at 5:00pm PT?

Below is a short excerpt from our playbook for context: 

--- excerpt ---
Retention: request/response payloads retained by default for 7 days in hosted mode (configurable). Ephemeral caches (KV) are cleared after session TTL; long-term storage requires explicit customer opt-in.
KMS: BYOK supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can opt into customer-managed key encryption for logs.
Subprocessors: logging infra, cloud provider, and a managed SFTP partner for exports. Full list will be sent.
--- end excerpt ---

We'll attach the operational playbook and a sample redaction/retention matrix in the follow-up. Sarah, please send the redline when ready.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-operational-playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@medisys.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
Cc: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Segregated-processing and derivative controls for LLM outputs

Alex — thanks for the quick response and the excerpt. Attaching our legal team's redline (Medisys_DPA_Redline_20261029.docx). A few clarifying points from Legal / InfoSec attached in the doc, but the high-priority operational items are: 

- Explicit "no-derivatives" language: Medisys will accept telemetry for service availability and aggregated usage metrics but wants an explicit prohibition on using prompt/response pairs or derived feature vectors for model improvement or training unless Medisys signs an opt-in addendum.
- Subprocessor residency: we see references to global logging and a managed export partner in Asia. We need to know whether any unredacted prompt/response pairs transit APAC subprocessors and, if so, what controls/contractual limits exist.
- Retention window: could Redwood commit to a default 30-day max retention for request/response in hosted mode for enterprise accounts, with the ability to shorten?
- KMS & BYOK: confirm if hosted can use customer-managed keys for long-term storage and exports.

We can be pragmatic on Dedicated/Private (deployment modes where data residency is explicit) but need these controls for hosted mode to proceed. If you can provide the playbook and the current subprocessor list + a short evidence pack (audit logs showing KV TTL and an example redaction run), we can route to sign-off faster.

I'll be on the 5:00pm PT call if you confirm — otherwise we can meet first thing tomorrow.

Best,
Sarah

Attachments: Medisys_DPA_Redline_20261029.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Medisys DPA redline — proposed response points

Alex / Rishi — quick internal notes before the call: 

- We should agree to a contractual "no-use-for-model-improvement" baseline for hosted enterprise accounts, with a narrow opt-in path for any tuning. Legal will want precise language but agreeing commercially speeds procurement.
- Operational evidence: Ops can produce a two-page artifact showing per-tenant KV scoping, TTL enforcement, and an exported subprocessor matrix. Recommend including a sample audit entry showing KV eviction after TTL.
- Residency: if Medisys needs APAC-free transit we can propose an onshore-only routing policy for their tenant (routing + logging in us-west/us-east regions). That avoids having to list APAC subprocessors for unredacted data.
- Retention ask (30 days): can accept for hosted enterprise if we allow a configurable retention lower bound and note exceptions for legal holds — include explicit process for expungement requests.

Proposed next-sentences for Sarah: commit to no-use-for-improvement by default; provide playbook & subprocessor list by EOD; propose call at 5pm PT to walk through redline. Rishi — can you prepare the sample audit log and one-pager on KMS options?

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
